summary:
Astro Alice – AI-Powered Astronaut Health and Well-being Companion

Astro Alice is an AI-powered companion designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. We developed an interactive AI application featuring Alice, an intelligent companion that provides emotional support, cognitive stimulation, and natural human-like conversations to help astronauts cope with isolation, stress, and the psychological challenges of living in confined space environments.

Alice engages astronauts through voice-based conversations, emotional check-ins, cognitive activities, brain exercises, and personalized interactions. Beyond companionship, the application aims to support astronaut well-being through health-focused features, activity tracking, reminders, and intelligent alerts.

Astro Alice addresses the challenge of maintaining astronauts' mental and physical well-being beyond Earth. During extended missions, limited human interaction and isolation can affect cognitive performance, emotional resilience, and overall health. By combining AI companionship with astronaut-focused health support, Astro Alice aims to make future space exploration safer, healthier, and more human-centered.
details:
Hi , my name is aiza and my project is based on human mental health.

What it does and how it works
Astro Alice is an AI companion for astronauts on long missions. Alice is a warm, playful conversational AI, shown as a glowing orb with eight states: idle, listening, thinking, speaking, happy, concerned, amused and alert. She talks with the astronaut by text or voice and runs short check-ins in the morning and evening. She also follows up on sleep and discomfort, and guides breathing exercises. She offers short mental activities such as word association, riddles, logic puzzles and reflection.

What makes Alice different is that she is connected to the astronaut’s health data. The health part of the app tracks heart rate, SpO₂, temperature, sleep, activity, nutrition and hydration, mood, stress, and cognitive tests. It compares recent days with the astronaut’s own baseline. When several indicators shift together, Alice mentions it gently, for example “I noticed your sleep and energy have changed lately, how are you really doing?” She never diagnoses. For urgent alerts she directs the astronaut to mission medical procedures. A read-only flight surgeon role can review the data and verify records, but cannot read Alice’s private conversations.

Benefits

  • Reduces isolation and gives crews a supportive, natural-sounding companion far from Earth.
  • Spots slow changes in wellbeing that are easy to miss, and raises them in a human way instead of a cold alert.
  • Keeps cognitive engagement going with short activities, and supports calm with guided breathing.
  • Puts the astronaut in control: Alice’s access to health data and her memory are both consent-based, editable and deletable.

Intended impact
To explore how an AI companion can support mental health and wellbeing on deep-space missions, with privacy and honesty built in. It is a prototype that other teams can build on, not a medical device.

Tools and technologies
HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single web page. Canvas for the animated orb and the procedural 3D Earth, SVG for charts, IndexedDB for local storage, and the Web Crypto API (AES-GCM) for optional passcode encryption. The browser’s speech features handle voice. Alice’s conversation uses Claude through the Anthropic API, with a built-in fallback for offline use. The app was built with the help of Claude and tested with Playwright in headless Chromium. It needs no special hardware.

Creativity

  • Alice has her own personality: playful and occasionally sarcastic, but never when the astronaut is distressed, and she avoids stock chatbot phrases.
  • Her orb expresses emotion through color, motion and pulse, and she sits above a procedurally generated Earth.
  • Her observations are framed as gentle questions, not conclusions, and she always says she may be wrong.

Factors considered
Safety (no diagnosis, escalation to mission medical procedures), consent and privacy (editable memory, audit log, optional encryption, a read-only surgeon role), honesty about data source (every demo measurement is labelled SIMULATED DATA), offline operation, and isolation and mental health in long missions. The app is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA, has not been medically validated, and connects to no real sensors or astronaut data.
